text.p: These are the leading stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- S E R B I A -
NASA BORBA
- U.S. President Bill Clinton has extended by another six months the freeze on the assets of Yugoslavia and the Bosnian Serb republic in the U.S.
- The National Bank of Yugoslavia has put a new 100-dinar note into circulation.
- Serbia's PTT sells 49 percent stake of Telecom Srbija to OTE of Greece and Stet of Italy.
- Council of economic reforms of the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia to discuss on Tuesday the working version of the privatisation law.
- Serbia may need to import sugar by March 1998 because only 58,000 hectares of sugarbeet were planted instead of the planned 100,000 ha.
- Belgrade high school teachers continue strike after failing to reach agreement with the government on Monday.
POLITIKA

- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic says the deal signed between PTT Srbije, Greek OTE and Italy's Stet will mark a big step towards Yugoslavia's dynamic economic integration in modern economic trends.
- Regional cooperation is a priority in Yugoslavia's political strategy, says foreign minister Milan Milutinovic at a conference of seven southeast European countries in Salonika.
- A 1.5 kilometer long and 15 metre wide oil slick on river Sava, first noticed on June 3, has disappeared.
DNEVNI TELEGRAF
- Changing Yugoslavia's constitution would marginalise Montenegro in the Yugoslav federation, says Montenegrin Parliament Speaker Svetozar Marovic.
- Serbian market inspectors on Monday closed Belgrade's largest open air market.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Federal government calls for extraordinary session of both houses of parliament on June 26 and 27. Agenda to include several laws on reforms, trade liberalisation, customs tariffs.
- Serb refugees say Croatian President Franjo Tudjman's remark during visit to Vukovar that not all Serbs can return to Croatia not reconciliatory.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Local Socialist Party of Serbia organisations support Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic's candidacy for President of Yugoslavia.
- Serbia will for the time being continue supplying Eastern Slavonia in Croatia with electricity.
- Serbian government submits to republican parliament draft law on local self-management, proportional election system.
- M O N T E N E G R O -
POBJEDA

- British ambassador in Belgrade Ivor Roberts has separate meetings with Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic, Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic and Parliament Speaker Svetozar Marovic. Marovic says the "proposed changes of the (Yugoslav) constitution will jeopardise the equality of federal units."

- Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) executive boards for Cetinje, Budva and Niksic oppose extraordinary party congress, Plav board supports it. Budva socialists say an extaordinary congress would be a smokescreen for the approval of proposed constitutional changes.

- Montenegrin police deny President Momir Bulatovic's allegations that ASI company was involved in illegal operations in which head of Montenegrin security Vukasin Maras took part, say no grounds for criminal charges.
